newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher but trail Wall St. gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher but trail Wall St. gains.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished higher on Friday, but trailed behind New York as weak gold shares restrained the Canadian market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 13.65 points to close at 4149.90 in turnover of 74 million shares valued at C$821 million (US$598 million).
Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners 478 to 365 with 298 issues ending flat.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 53 points after a U.S. payrolls report calmed investors' inflation fears.
In Canada, the unemployment rate returned to a more usual level of 9.4 percent in August after jumping to 10 percent in June.
"Toronto had a sympathy rise with New York, but we didn't push into new high territory," said Ron Meisels, president of Montreal-based P & C Holdings Ltd.
The precious metals group lost 62 points as COMEX December gold finished down US$0.80 at US$388.80 an ounce.
Gold prices have dropped steadily for the past eight days and the market ignored today's payrolls report, gold traders said.
Toronto's strong side was led by financial services, communications, transportation and forestry products.
* Fairfax Financial soared 32 to close at 230, a new high.
The financial services firm said it plans to acquire the reinsurance unit of French insurer GAN for US$137.9 million.
* Newbridge Networks Corp. extended its recent rally, rising 3.80 to 87.70. The technology stock received a boost from favourable analysts' reports following the company's annual meeting on Thursday.
* Among gold shares, Barrick Gold Corp. dropped 0.30 to 37.20, while Placer Dome Inc. surrendered 0.20 to 32.90.
Junior gold miner Bre-X Minerals Ltd. bucked the trend, adding 0.90 to 25.95 on 1.3 million shares.
* Canadian Pacific Ltd. climbed 0.10 to 30.95 on 410,000 shares. The conglomerate said it will sell most of its Canadian real estate arm to Oxford Properties Group Inc. for US$694 million).
* Blue Range Resource Corp. topped the most-active list, closing unchanged at 7.50 on 1.67 million shares.
